question: The root header's Sources field names hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.md and hsdd/context/update-1-add-phone.md, both superseded by PRD v2. How does the citation touch move them?

options.label: both collapse into the PRD v2 path
options.consequence: The field reads hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.v2.md, hsdd/context/rfc-simple-login.md. Every source the root lists governs it now; no superseded path stays in a live field.

options.label: PRD v2 added, baselines kept beside it
options.consequence: The field would list documents that no longer govern the root, against hsdd-spec's 'No node's Sources lists a document that does not govern it', and the file would keep a baseline path, so cites-superseded would keep holding for it.

chosen: both collapse into the PRD v2 path
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch names 'a node's Sources entry for a source document' as a live citation that moves to the current version. PRD v2's header says it supersedes prd-simple-login.md together with update-1-add-phone.md, so one PRD v2 entry replaces both; the intake record's Sources and Scope paragraph says the same ('each citation touch moves the PRD 1 and Update 1 entries to it'). The root's field lists paths without sections, so no section mapping arises. RFC-001 is current (version 1, normative) and stays.

question: The root's ## Sources lists hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.md as 'PRD (approved) · product scope, user stories US-1 to US-3 with their acceptance criteria, screens, demo accounts, team and delivery, success criteria' and has no Update 1 entry (Q-026). What does the moved entry say, and do the superseded documents keep a line?

options.label: one PRD v2 entry, its line restated, no history line
options.consequence: The entry reads `hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.v2.md` · PRD v2 (approved) · product scope, user stories US-1 to US-6 with their acceptance criteria, screens, demo accounts, rooms, constraints, what it leaves to engineering, team and delivery, success criteria. The inventory lists what governs the tree now; the missing Update 1 entry stops mattering because PRD v2 carries its content. The chain back to PRD 1 and Update 1 stays in PRD v2's own Supersedes line and in the intake records.

options.label: PRD v2 entry plus a superseded line for PRD 1 and Update 1
options.consequence: The inventory also names the two baseline documents as superseded, informative only, not decomposed. It keeps both baseline paths in the root file, so the cites-superseded condition holds for it permanently, and 'not decomposed' would be untrue of documents that were decomposed.

options.label: path moved, line kept as written
options.consequence: The entry would say PRD v2 governs user stories US-1 to US-3 only and name none of rooms, constraints or what it leaves to engineering, which PRD v2's text makes false.

chosen: one PRD v2 entry, its line restated, no history line
why: The ## Sources entry is a live statement of what each source governs, so its path moves. The old line 'user stories US-1 to US-3' is false for PRD v2, which has US-1 to US-6 plus Rooms, Constraints and Left to engineering sections that bind the tree (booking-api@v1's limits and ADR-001's restart answer come from the last), so the sentence is restated from PRD v2's section list (hsdd-spec: restate a sentence the new version makes false). Dropping the baselines follows the intake record ('each citation touch moves the PRD 1 and Update 1 entries to it'); the run treats them as baseline sources read only to see what changed, not as inputs that govern. A history line would have led if a shipped phase resolved 'the PRD' through the root's inventory rather than naming the document or its intake record in its own Scope.
evidence: PRD v2 (User stories, Rooms, Constraints, Left to engineering, Team and delivery, Success)
.claude/skills/hsdd-spec/SKILL.md (Touch and Citation Touch; Process step 1, Inventory the sources)

question: The embedded summaries of simple-login.backend, simple-login.web and simple-login.integration in the root file carry Sources lines naming PRD 1 and Update 1 with sections. Q-032, Q-038 and Q-046 leave 'the Sources field in both places' to H11 to H13. Who moves the embedded copies, and to which PRD v2 sections?

options.label: move them here, each section to its PRD v2 counterpart
options.consequence: Each copy gets one PRD v2 entry holding the counterparts of its PRD 1 and Update 1 sections (Update 1's AC-2.1 amended and AC-2.4 are PRD v2 AC-2.1 and AC-2.4, its Screen is Screens); sections that newly govern a node (US-4 to US-6, Rooms, AC-2.5) are not added, since the intake record gives them to each node's phase-plan-append. The copies equal what H11 to H13 write if they apply the same mapping; hsdd-reconcile's version ripple (H15, H17, H19) makes each copy match its node's header in any case.

options.label: move them here and add every PRD v2 section that now governs the node
options.consequence: The copies would be complete for PRD v2 at once, but they would run ahead of the children's own headers, which gain those sections only at H14, H16 and H18, and the citation touch would be adding citations rather than moving them.

options.label: leave them to H11 to H13
options.consequence: Not possible: a citation-touch on a node writes only that node's file (hsdd/scripts/auto/lib/kinds.mjs writeSet), so no later step in this block could move them before the reconciles, and the root would keep live baseline paths until H15.

chosen: move them here, each section to its PRD v2 counterpart
why: The copies sit in the touched file, and a node's Sources entry for a source document is a live citation the rule moves; the rule's carve-out for copies above a node covers contract versions in Produces and Consumes only. H11 to H13 cannot write this file (their write set is the node's own spec), so the earlier steps' 'both places' cannot be done there; this step does it and routes the mapping to each so the headers can match. A move keeps what the citation pointed at: backend (US-1, US-2, Demo accounts, Scope); web (US-1, US-2, US-3, Screens, Scope), Scope coming from Update 1; integration (Success, Team and delivery, Constraints, Demo accounts, AC-2.1, AC-2.4), Constraints decided separately. Adding the newly governing sections is the phase-plan-append's job by the intake record and hsdd-phase-plan's Change Requests rule, and reconcile carries them up.
evidence: PRD v2 US-2, Screens, Demo accounts, Scope
Update 1 1 Change, Screen, Demo accounts, Scope

question: simple-login.integration's embedded Sources cites PRD 1 Team and delivery, which held both 'one backend developer builds the service; one frontend developer builds the web app' and 'Local demo only for now: both run on a developer laptop'. PRD v2 keeps the first in Team and delivery and moves the second to Constraints ('Local laptop only, as before'). Which PRD v2 sections does the moved citation name?

options.label: Team and delivery and Constraints
options.consequence: The moved entry still points at both statements it pointed at before. Constraints also carries PostgreSQL 17 under Docker Compose and the real-database test rule, which already govern the node (its Owns and Isolation strategy cite PRD v2 Constraints).

options.label: Team and delivery only, by heading
options.consequence: The entry keeps its headings one to one, but no longer points at the local-laptop statement the integration node's run scripts rest on; H18's phase-plan-append would have to add Constraints.

why: A citation move keeps the content a citation pointed at, and PRD v2 split PRD 1's Team and delivery across two sections. Constraints is already cited by the node's own text (S11, DEC-098), so naming it in Sources lists nothing that does not govern the node. Had PRD v2's Team and delivery still held the laptop line, the heading-only move would have led.

question: The Overview's Assumption line cites '(AC-1.2)' with no document, written when PRD 1 was the only PRD; PRD v2 AC-1.2 has the same text. Qualify it or leave it bare?

options.label: qualify as PRD v2 AC-1.2
options.consequence: The line reads '"same message, never says which was wrong" (PRD v2 AC-1.2) extends to timing, as the RFC's section 4 states.' It matches the other bullets of the same list, which S08 restated to cite PRD v2 by section; the quoted words are PRD v2's.

options.label: leave AC-1.2 bare
options.consequence: It resolves through the root's Sources, which now lists PRD v2 only, so it is not wrong; but it is the one PRD citation in the list without a document, and a reader comparing with PRD 1 cannot tell which was meant.

why: The citation was written against PRD 1 and is live (the assumption still governs the backend's timing rule). PRD v2 AC-1.2 is word for word PRD 1's, so the sentence stays true and only the citation moves. Consistency with the restated bullets beside it (DEC-067) decided it; had the list's other bullets cited bare ids, leaving it bare would have led.

question: The Decomposition axis says 'The PRD answers "who builds what?": one backend developer builds the service, one frontend developer builds the web app, and they ship separately.' PRD v2 Team and delivery keeps this and adds that the backend developer owns the database (Q-026). Move the citation only, or also restate the clause?

options.label: move the citation, keep the clause
options.consequence: The sentence reads 'PRD v2 answers "who builds what?" (Team and delivery): one backend developer builds the service, one frontend developer builds the web app, and they ship separately.' True against PRD v2; the database's owner stays stated where S08 put it, in the Decisions section citing PRD v2 Team and delivery.

options.label: move the citation and add 'and owns the database'
options.consequence: The axis paragraph repeats the owner fact in full. It goes beyond what the citation touch needs: the sentence is not false under PRD v2, and the Decisions section and simple-login.backend's Owns already state the database's owner.

chosen: move the citation, keep the clause
why: hsdd-spec restates a sentence in a citation touch when the new version makes it false; this one stays true, since PRD v2 Team and delivery still has the same two developers building the service and the web app in parallel and shipping separately, which is the axis. The database clause adds no node and no owner (Inside each node one person owns everything stays true), and the root states it already (Decisions, DEC-067). Had no sentence in the root named the database's owner, adding the clause here would have led.

question: OQ1's detail opens 'The PRD scopes delivery to a local demo, and the RFC (section 9) relies on the Vite dev proxy ...'. PRD v2 has no 'local demo only' line: it says 'Local laptop only, as before' (Constraints) and lists 'deployment beyond the laptop' as out (Scope). How does the sentence read after the move?

options.label: restate in PRD v2's words
options.consequence: 'PRD v2 keeps delivery on the local laptop (Constraints) and puts deployment beyond it out of scope (Scope), and the RFC (section 9) relies on ...'. Each clause is a PRD v2 statement with its section; the RFC clause is unchanged.

options.label: swap the document only
options.consequence: 'PRD v2 scopes delivery to a local demo, and ...'. Shortest change, but 'local demo' is PRD 1's phrase (Team and delivery); PRD v2 states the scope as a laptop constraint and an out-of-scope item, so the sentence would cite PRD v2 for words it does not use.

why: The sentence states what holds now, so its citation moves; it then has to be true against PRD v2's text, and PRD v2 frames the limit as 'Local laptop only, as before' (Constraints) and 'deployment beyond the laptop' out (Scope). What it said: the PRD scopes delivery to a local demo. What it says now: PRD v2 keeps delivery on the local laptop and puts deployment beyond it out of scope. It follows PRD v2 Constraints and Scope. The RFC-001 §9 clause is current and unchanged.

question: OQ1's detail says 'Nothing in v1 is contingent on it', v1 being the product's version 1 (PRD 1). Under PRD v2, move it, keep it as history, or change OQ1's status?

options.label: move to PRD v2, OQ1 stays OPEN
options.consequence: 'Nothing in PRD v2 is contingent on it; it is recorded so the next change that deploys the product starts from a named question.' The table row is unchanged: OPEN, waits on ext: product, affects simple-login.integration and simple-login.web.

options.label: keep 'v1' as history
options.consequence: The sentence would describe only the superseded version and say nothing about whether the current one depends on the question, which is what the paragraph is for.

options.label: move it and mark OQ1 resolved
options.consequence: Would claim PRD v2 answered the deployment question; it did not, it only keeps deployment beyond the laptop out of scope.

chosen: move to PRD v2, OQ1 stays OPEN
why: The sentence is a live statement that the question blocks nothing now, so its version reference moves. It stays true: PRD v2 Constraints keeps the product on the laptop and PRD v2 Scope puts deployment beyond the laptop out, so the Vite dev proxy still gives one origin and nothing waits on OQ1. PRD v2 names no deployment target, so the question is neither answered nor narrowed and stays OPEN with product as the external party. A PRD v2 criterion that needed a second origin would have changed the status.

question: The Decisions section's RFC-001 bullet opens 'RFC-001 was written for version 1.', which names the superseded version string 1. Move it or keep it?

options.label: keep as history
options.consequence: The bullet keeps saying what RFC-001 was written for; the rest of it already says which of its statements PRD v2 overtakes and that its authors are asked to amend it (DEC-013). The superseded string 1 stays in the file in this one sentence.

options.label: rewrite to name PRD v2
options.consequence: The sentence would lose its point: it explains why RFC-001's two endpoints, no database and no router no longer hold, and that is a fact about the version RFC-001 was written for.

why: hsdd-spec's citation touch keeps the version historical text describes, an account of what an earlier version did among them; this sentence is that account, and RFC-001's own header ('Implements: PRD: Simple Login', prd-simple-login.md) bears it out. The other matches of the bare token 1 in the file are not citations of a version: RFC-001 §1 (twice in the embedded summaries, once in the Decisions bullet) is a section of a current source, and 'Lane 1' is a dev-flow lane.

question: The root cites profile-api@v1 ten times (the Isolation strategy, the three child-table rows, the three embedded Produces and Consumes lines, the DAG edge, the dependency table and the contract matrix). profile-api@v1 is stable, not deprecated, coexisting with v2. Which node receives the one consider item the rule asks for?

options.label: simple-login.backend, the producer
options.consequence: The item reaches the backend's next step (H11, then its planning and reconcile, H14 and H15). The producer's plan already serves v2 only on GET /api/me from simple-login.backend.3, so what is left is the deprecation of its contract, the execution plan's C-1, which waits on Sync A's A-1 (DEC-016).

options.label: simple-login.web, a consumer
options.consequence: The web's shipped web.1 and web.3 consumed v1 and web.4 moved to v2; its own Overview's profile-api@v1 citation already went to H12 (Q-038), so the item would repeat that one.

options.label: run
options.consequence: Puts the item before the owner at the align or report, where A-1 is decided, but the rule routes a coexisting version to a node so that node's planning decides when it moves.

why: hsdd-spec routes one consider item to the producer or consumer the citing sentence is about. The root's Isolation strategy is about all three children; every phase that names v1 is shipped (backend.2, web.1, web.3, integration.1, each with a verification doc on main), and every unshipped consumer is on v2, so no consumer's plan has a move left to make. The producer owns profile-api's file, and its deprecation is the one act that turns these citations into superseded ones (the intake record's insert rule then adds a citation-touch on the root). Every copy of a Produces or Consumes line is reconcile's to write in any case. Had a consumer still planned a phase on v1, that consumer would have led.

question: How does this citation touch classify against the touched artifact's own versioning rules?

options.label: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
options.consequence: A node spec carries no version of its own. The touch changes Sources entries and the sentences four citations sit in; no node, contract id, Produces or Consumes line, Governed by line, edge, open-question status or decision changes, and neither registry needs regenerating.

options.label: a structural change to the root
options.consequence: Would ask for a spec-touch or reconcile to re-check the decomposition, though no node, contract or edge changed.

chosen: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
why: hsdd-spec asks for the classification as one decision. The root's Kind, Consumes, Produces, Governed by, Decomposes into, child set, DAG, contract matrix and OQ1's status are byte for byte as before; only citations of PRD 1 and Update 1 and the sentences that hold them changed, each restatement recorded on its own (DEC-106, DEC-111). No contract or ADR file changed, so hsdd/contract/INDEX.md and hsdd/adr/INDEX.md are left as they are.

question: S12, the citation touch on the root, also moved the Sources lines in the three embedded child summaries, which the children's own citation touches (H11 to H13) cannot write because their write set is the child's file only. Keep it, or revert those three lines?

options.label: Keep it
options.consequence: The root's copies cite PRD v2 now; H11 to H13 get the exact mapping as consider items so each child's header matches its copy, and reconcile's ripple later recopies the headers anyway.

options.label: Revert the three copies
options.consequence: The root keeps citing PRD 1 and Update 1 in its child summaries until reconcile runs, and no step in the block is able to move them before that.

why: The root's file is this step's write set and the copies are its text; leaving them would keep superseded source paths in the root with no step able to move them before H15. The mapping is routed so the children's own headers agree. A child citation touch able to write its embedded copy would have changed this.
